history.title: Illinois Transitional Bilingual Education Act enacted (PA 78-727)
history.description: Public Act 78-727 created Article 14C of the Illinois School Code (105 ILCS 5/14C), one of the strongest state TBE mandates in the country. Article 14C requires any public school attendance center with 20 or more EL students of the same language background to operate a Transitional Bilingual Education program for at least three years per student, and any school with fewer than 20 to provide a Transitional Program of Instruction (TPI) — i.e., ESL-based services. The 1973 statute is the legal source of Illinois's bilingual-and-ESL endorsement structure and of the state's bilingual-teacher Type-29 credential lineage that 23 IAC Part 25 later modernized. Illinois followed Massachusetts (1971), New Mexico (1973), and Texas (1973) in mandating bilingual instruction by statute.

history.title: Illinois adopts State Seal of Biliteracy (PA 098-0560)
history.description: Illinois became one of the first states to authorize a State Seal of Biliteracy on high-school diplomas, certifying graduates' proficiency in English and one or more world languages. ISBE administers the program with district-level participation; the affordance is now embedded in graduation pathways and feeds into the Bilingual/ESL teacher pipeline.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Illinois's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: 23 IAC 24.140 supersedes 24.130 as Illinois Professional Teaching Standards
history.description: ISBE's revised Illinois Professional Teaching Standards (23 IAC 24.140) take effect 2026-07-01, replacing 23 IAC 24.130. The new standards drop the explicit 'English language learners' phrasing that 24.130 carried, shifting EL-relevant competencies under broader 'diverse learners' language. Flag for re-coding `professionalStandardsMentions.el` after the transition.

elPercentHistory.note: Illinois State Board of Education, October fall snapshot (332,936 EL students of approximately 1,800,000 enrolled). Identification via home language survey plus WIDA screening within 30 days. The ISBE figure runs approximately 3.6 percentage points above NCES's fall 2021 value (12.8%); part of the divergence reflects documented enrollment growth (ISBE attributes recent growth to families escaping global conflicts), and part may reflect that the ISBE count includes students in the post-reclassification monitoring period whereas NCES does not.
